text:
incident-bot: ALERT triggered: autoscale-pool-saturation (severity: page)
incident-bot: metric=queue_depth per-shard > 120 for 3m, tokens/sec dropped 40%, throttle_events increased
maya: ack — I'm on it, switching to on-call context. grabbing dashboard now :eyes:
sam: seeing a spike in queue depth across gpu-pool-2, lots of throttles. customers reporting high latency (frontend 500ms+)
jordan: any correlated deploys? I don't see recent git pushes to runtime in last 6h.
maya: no deploys. Looks like gradual token/sec drop then sharp queue buildup. Could be a hot model or cache invalidation.
leah: pushing a zoom link in #incident-ops. Also pinging platform to allow scale-up if needed.
ops-bot: autoscaler: observed scale-up suppressed by max_instances=12 on gpu-pool-2. current_instances=12, target=20
maya: that explains it. I'm going to temporarily raise max_instances to 20 to relieve queue. doing it now.
maya: runbook command:
```
/infra-cli set-pool-max gpu-pool-2 --max-instances 20 --reason "mitigate saturating queue during incident"
```
ops-bot: acknowledged — pool gpu-pool-2 max_instances updated to 20
sam: queue depth dropping within a minute, throttle events down from ~120/min to ~30/min :thumbsup:
jordan: can we also mute noisy alerts? autoscale-pool-saturation is firing a lot; it's drowning other alerts.
maya: yep muting now for 30m, will create a suppress/route so it pages only if 429 rate > 5% for 5m.
maya: changing alert rule snippet (proposed):
```
- alert: autoscale-pool-saturation
  expr: (sum(queue_depth) by (pool) > 150 && increase(throttle_events[5m]) > 50) || (increase(429_responses[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m]) > 0.05)
  for: 5m
```
leah: that looks much better. We should also add tokens/sec drop as an early-warning but not page unless coupled with 429s.
sam: agreed — tokens/sec low is noisy when model warmups happen. add a dashboard tile for tokens/sec per-pool with median + p95 overlay.
jordan: created a quick dashboard panel: link=https://grafana.company/r/d/abcd/autoscale-signals showing queue depth, tokens/sec, throttle_events, 429_rate per pool
maya: creating a follow-up ticket for post-incident tuning: SUMMARY: adjust autoscale thresholds, add dashboard, and run synthetic load tests. assigning to eng-sre and eng-runtime.
maya: ticket link: https://jira.company/browse/INF-7123
ops-bot: incident status: mitigation in progress — queue stabilized, throttles decreased, latency improving
sam: contacting CS to ask about customer impact windows and any open support tickets. cc @customer-success
leah: quick note for the postmortem — consider increasing burst-capacity window or enabling temporary burst policy when pool hits >90% for 2m instead of immediate paging.
maya: agreed. Also propose adding a geared fallback model route for heavy requests so we can shed load gracefully.
jordan: thanks all. leaving the mute for 30m. will follow up in the ticket with graphs and thresholds we tested.
maya: handing off to next oncall @oncall-rotation — summary: temporary max_instances increased to 20 on gpu-pool-2, alert rule softened (now requires 429% trigger), dashboard added, follow-up ticket INF-7123. if regressions occur re-open the page.
oncall-rotation: ack — taking over. will monitor for the next 45m and coordinate with eng-runtime for any further config changes.
sam: final check — any user-facing mitigation we should communicate? if not, I'll mark customer-impact as "degraded" for thirty minutes and loop CS.
leah: CS says two customers reported latency, no data loss. set impact = degraded, timeline 00:12–00:42 UTC (approx)
maya: closing incident thread, will draft postmortem with timeline and alert-tuning recommendations.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — duration ~34m — responders: maya, sam, jordan, leah — follow-up: INF-7123
